transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because no matter what anyone says, I know some people at work are secretly working together to set me up, and nobody seems to take that seriously. It's incredibly frustrating because everyone else just brushes it off, but I know exactly what they are trying to do to me.
Besides feeling that people at work are plotting against you, have you been hearing voices or noticing your thoughts or speech becoming confused or hard to follow? If so, when did that start?

No, my mind is completely clear and I definitely don't hear any voices or have confused thoughts. Outside of this sabotage at work, I function perfectly normally—I do my inspections by the book, pay my bills, and hang out with my brothers on weekends. The only issue is the actual setup happening at my workplace, which is very real.
How long have you been convinced that your coworkers are plotting against you? Did this start suddenly over days to weeks, or has it been going on for several months or longer?

This has been going on for about a year now, so it wasn't a sudden thing that happened overnight. It started gradually, right around the time a senior driver publicly challenged my authority after that county bus collision. Since then, I've watched the pieces fall into place and I know they are targeting me.

During this past year, have you also had long periods of feeling very depressed or unusually energetic with much less need for sleep? If yes, did those mood changes happen at the same time as your belief about your coworkers?

No, I haven't experienced any of those mood swings or changes in my energy levels. My mood has been completely fine, and my only real stress or focus is dealing with what those people at work are doing to me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a persistent, non-bizarre persecutory delusion lasting about one year, with otherwise preserved functioning and no evidence of hallucinations, disorganized thought, or prominent mood episodes. This pattern is most consistent with delusional disorder, persecutory type.
